This section summarizes the activities completed to manufacture the structured sorbent filters. Electrically Conductive Nonwoven An 8” x 5” conductive filter sample was placed on a stand with electrodes connected along the length of the filter sample. A copper film was adhered to each end using silver paste, which provides electric current distribution along the width of the filter sample. The power modulation was controlled using a silicone- controlled rectifier (SCR) connected to a variable voltage transformer, and the temperature was measured using an IR sensor. The temperature and resistance were measured throughout the experiment, where resistance measurements were conducted at the end of the measurement cycle. Prior to resistance measurement, the sample was allowed to cool to room temperature to avoid variability due to temperature. One hundred joule-heating cycles were performed showing stable resistance throughout all 100 cycles. Coated HCSS testing As part of an initial assessment, activity 2, an 8”x11” sample of the electrically conductive nonwoven substrate and was coated with Susteon’s sorbent and tested. The heating stability of the sorbent coated filter substrate was tested using the same apparatus and operating conditions as described above. A total of 500 Joule-heated thermal cycles were completed, showing no change in the heating performance. These results further verify that electrically resistive filter substrate can be used for the DAC application. The sorbent coated filter was then tested to confirm that the sorbent could be regenerated by resistively heating the electrically conductive nonwoven. A sample of the sorbent coated nonwoven was placed into a reactor cell with each end of the sample connected to an electrode. A SCR was used to modulate the voltage applied along the electrodes, and the surface temperature of the filter was used as temperature feedback control. The sample was tested using simulated DAC conditions from the lab screening reactor. The results (Figure 6, left) show short-term sorbent stability and confirm the repeatability of the adsorption/desorption sequence using the sorbent-coated filter. The resistance of the sample was calculated at 70°C based on the steady-state voltage applied to the sample and steady-state current measured during the isothermal hold.
